justifications.functional_suitability: The Scoring Engine handles R-01 (approve/decline/review decisions), the Case Management API and Fraud Analyst SPA satisfy R-02 (case management), and the Rule & Model Distribution Service together with atomic pointer swaps in the Evaluation Engine addresses R-03 without downtime.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Achieving sub-50ms at P99 under 3,000 rps is supported by in-memory Go evaluation, ElastiCache Redis feature store, ALB with mTLS/gRPC, and asynchronous audit streaming via Amazon EventBridge, offloading heavy write paths.
justifications.compatibility: Supports Payment Gateway via HTTPS/gRPC over TLS 1.3 and external ML providers via HTTPS/S3. However, direct integration mechanisms with external card networks/tokenization services for detokenization/PAN handling are vague beyond stripping tokens in the Scoring API Controller.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are well-served via the Fraud Analyst SPA featuring the Case Review Workspace Module, Analytics Dashboard Module, and Explainability Renderer, while Risk Operations Managers access audit logs through dedicated APIs.
justifications.reliability: Circuit breaking in Scoring API Controller and DLQs in the event bus protect reliability. However, R-07's requirement that payments must not be blocked for >1 minute during scoring unavailability lacks an explicit automated fallback/fail-open bypass mechanism.
justifications.security: R-05 and PCI-DSS compliance are rigorously supported via token stripping, mTLS, AWS Cognito with WAF, Ed25519 bundle signing, and tamper-evident audit storage in Aurora PostgreSQL using SHA-256 chaining and S3 Glacier Object Lock (WORM).
justifications.maintainability: Excellent modular decomposition into loosely coupled microservices (Scoring Engine, Case Management API, Rule & Model Distribution Service) orchestrated via EventBridge, enabling a 3-engineer team to maintain, test, and deploy services independently.
justifications.portability: Targeted specifically at AWS eu-west-1 using ECS Fargate, Aurora, and ElastiCache. Heavy reliance on proprietary AWS services (Cognito, EventBridge, KMS, S3 Glacier Object Lock) limits cross-cloud portability, though well-adapted to the target cloud.

PERF-01.justification: The Scoring Engine is implemented in Go on ECS Fargate using in-memory model evaluation with atomic pointer swaps and concurrent Redis feature fetching. Audit dispatch is decoupled asynchronously via EventBridge, ensuring the P99 latency stays well within the 50 ms target at 3,000 requests per second.
sensitivity_points: ElastiCache Redis read latency under peak concurrent lookups
Stateless Go container CPU utilization during in-memory evaluation
tradeoffs: In-memory evaluation sacrifices cross-node model synchronization for predictable microsecond execution

PERF-02.justification: Analyst workloads are physically separated from payment scoring. Authorizations enter via an Application Load Balancer to Go scoring containers, while analyst UI traffic flows via Amazon API Gateway to a separate Case Management container backed by Aurora read replicas and Redis caching.
sensitivity_points: Aurora read-replica replication lag during heavy batch updates
Network isolation between analyst queries and the scoring pipeline
tradeoffs: Using read replicas introduces eventual consistency for analyst views while isolating transaction latency

AVAIL-01.justification: While the Scoring API Controller includes a circuit breaker, the architecture lacks an autonomous upstream fallback engine at the ALB/Ingress level when Scoring Engine instances crash completely, leaving fallback decision generation and auditing under full service outages ambiguously specified.
sensitivity_points: Placement and behavior of fallback decision logic when scoring tasks terminate
tradeoffs: Implementing fallbacks at the ingress layer preserves availability but restricts access to rich fraud features

AVAIL-02.justification: Scoring does not write synchronously to Aurora PostgreSQL. The Audit Dispatcher streams signed payloads asynchronously over EventBridge, supported by SQS Dead-Letter Queues and native Event Archives, isolating scoring from database slowdowns or outages while guaranteeing audit preservation.
sensitivity_points: EventBridge client buffer size and SDK retry timeout settings
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit dispatch introduces eventual persistence consistency to protect real-time decision throughput

MOD-01.justification: The Rule & Model Distribution Service signs and publishes model bundles to S3. Scoring engine instances hot-reload verified bundles in background threads and activate them instantly via in-memory atomic pointer swaps with zero downtime, embedding the model version in every decision payload.
sensitivity_points: Thread-safe atomic pointer swapping during concurrent evaluation execution
Polling latency of Rule Synchronizer across container instances
tradeoffs: In-memory atomic swaps briefly duplicate model memory footprints during rolling updates

MOD-02.justification: Rule updates pass static syntax linting and cryptographic signing before distribution via S3. Scoring instances synchronize rules within seconds without restart, Redis provides state for velocity checks, and decision outputs explicitly log rule IDs and evaluation factors for explainability.
sensitivity_points: Rule syntax validation coverage against unhandled runtime evaluation exceptions
tradeoffs: Strict static linting prevents runtime execution crashes but restricts dynamic custom scripting

SEC-01.justification: Token stripping and external tokenization prevent clear-text PAN exposure in the analyst workspace and storage. However, the architecture omits explicit automated anomaly detection or alerting mechanisms (e.g., SIEM, GuardDuty) to detect and notify of compromised analyst accounts within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of strict token stripping before persistence and analyst display
Absence of behavioral anomaly detection on Cognito/API access logs
tradeoffs: Restricting analyst views to tokenized metadata prevents data leaks but limits manual transaction verification

SEC-02.justification: The architecture utilizes PL/pgSQL cryptographic chaining, append-only ledger mechanisms, and lifecycle archiving to AWS S3 Glacier with WORM Object Lock for 7-year retention. The Audit Query Gateway provides batch hydration and pre-signed retrieval well within one working day.
sensitivity_points: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval restoration initiation latency
Integrity verification of SHA-256 cryptographic audit chains over archived partitions
tradeoffs: Archiving to Glacier WORM storage drastically lowers long-term infrastructure costs while introducing asynchronous retrieval delays
